caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 388 of 2009
lawyer:
Omar Sadat; Advocate (appeared with the leave of the Court) Instructed by Mrs. Sulia Khatun Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner
Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, Senior Advocate Instructed by Zainul Ahedin, Advocate-on-Record ----- Respondents
parties:
Bank of Credit and Commerce ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Sufia Re-Rolling and Steel Mills Ltd. Dhaka and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
B.K. Das J.:- This petition for leave to appeal has arisen against the judgment and order dated 2.12.2008 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 6254 of 2008 (Analogously heard with Writ Petition No. 7346 of 2007 and disposed of by a common judgment) disposing of the writ petition directing Artha Rin Adalat No. 3 Dhaka to dispose of Money Execution Case No. 51 of 1992 filed by the decree-holder after deduction of the decreetal amount payable to the decree-holder Bank from the decreetal amount payable by the decree-holder Bank in Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1999 pending before the Artha Rin Adalat, 3rd Court, Dhaka and also directed the Joint District Judge 3rd Court., Dhaka to start execution proceeding in Money Execution Case No. 03 of 1999 for realization of the decreetal amount which would remain after deduction of the decreetal amount payable to the decree-holder Bank. 

 2. Sufia Re-Rolling and Steel Mills Ltd. through its Managing Director and 5 other directors have filed Writ Petition No. 7346 of 2007 against Bank of Credit & Commerce at present Eastern. Bank Ltd. Head office and its managing Director challenging an auction notice published in daily newspaper in Money Execution Case No. 51 of 1992 of Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka while the Eastern Bank Ltd. has filed writ Petition No. 6254 of 2008 against the aforesaid Sufia Re-Rolling & Steel Mills Ltd. and its managing director and other directors challenging the part of the decree passed on 17.1.1991 in Title Suit No. 219 of 1.987 of Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No.1, Dhaka and also the order dated 11.5.2008 passed in Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1999 of the Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka. The said Title Suit No. 219 of 1987 against Sufia Re-Rolling & Steel Mills Ltd. and its directors for realiyation of loan and that suit was ultimately decreed for an amount of Tk. 75,06,904.69 with interest at the rate of 18% from the date of filing of the suit till the date of passing of the decree. During continuation of that Title Suit No. 219 of 1987 Sufia Re-Rolling & Steel Mills Ltd. and its directors filed Money Suit No.  47 of 1991 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka against the Bank of Credit & Commerce (now Eastern Bank Ltd.) for realization of Tk.68,6995851/21. Title Suit No. 47 of 1991 was decreed on 11.1.1999 for an amount of Tk. 2,85,24,630.21 with interest at the rate of 18% till realization of the decreetal amount. Against the said decree the judgment debtor bank filed E No.108 of 1999 in the High Court Division which was allowed in part on 31.8.2004 and the decreetal amount was reduced to taka 43,22,114.21 with interest at the rate of 18% from the date of filing of the suit till realization. The plaintiff Sufia Re-Rolling & Steel Mills Ltd. and others then filed Civil petition for leave to appeal No. 1556 of 2004 before the Appellate Division against the judgment passed in EA. No. 108 of 1999 but the said leave petition was dismissed on 5.8.2007. The decree-holder plaintiff Bank of Title Suit No. 219 of 1987 filed Title Execution Case No. 51 of 1992 for realization of the decretal amount and in that title execution case notice for auction of the mortgaged property was published on 10.8.2007 and at that stage the judgment-debtor Sufia Re-Rolling & Steel Mills Ltd. and others filed Writ Petition No. 7346 of 2007 before the High Court Division and obtained rule and also an order of stay of further proceeding of Title Execution Case No. 51 of 1992. Sufia Re-Roiling and still Mills Ltd. and its Directors, who are the decree-holders in Money Suit No. 47 of 1991, filed Execution Case being Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1999 in the 3rd Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for realisation of the decreetal amount along with interest who rejected the claim for set off by the impugned order dated 11.5.2008 holding that since both the execution cases were pending in two different courts, set off was not possible. Thereafter on 18.8.2008 the decree holder bank filed Writ Petition No. 6254 of 2008 challenging the decree dated 17.1.1991 passed in Title Suit No. 219 of 1987 exonerating the defendants from paying the interest till the date of realization of decreetal amount and also the order dated 11.5.2008 passed in Money Execution Cases No. 3 of 1999 rejecting the bank's application for set off. Rule was issued in this Writ Petition on 18.8.2008 and on that date an order also was passed staying all further proceedings of Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1999. 

 3. The learned Judges of the High Court Division noticed "From the above stated admitted facts it is evident that both the sets of Writ Petitioners have got one decree for money each against the other. Admittedly the Writ Petitioner Eastern Bank Limited has got a decree for an amount of TK. 75,00,904/- with interest at the rate of Tk.18% from the date of filing of the suit till the date of passing of the decree. The borrower Sufia Re-Rolling & Steel Mills Ltd. also admittedly has .got a decree for Tk. 43, 22,114.21 with interest at the rate of Tk. 18% from the date of filing of the suit till realization of decreetal amount payable to the Writ Petitioners Sufia Re-Rolling & Steel Mills Ltd. is not fixed rather, it is increasing day by day. And undisputedly the decreetal amount payable to Sufia Re-Rolling & Steel Mills Ltd. has grown up by this time, much more than the decreetal amount payable to Eastern Bank Limited." The High Court Division further noticed "However, since both the contesting parties before us have got a decree for money against the other party we asked both the parties to make a settlement themselves, but in-spite of taking some time from us for making settlement both of them failed to reach any settlement and they have prayed for an equitable order from this court to settle the matter. We have considered facts and circumstances deeply. The decretal amount payable to the Writ Petitioner Sufia Re-Rolling & Steel Mills Ltd. has increased much more than the decreetal amount payable to the Writ Petition Eastern Bank Limited and this amount is increasing day by day. In this circumstances we find it just and proper to deduct the decretal amount payable to the Writ Petitioners Eastern Bank Limited as this amount is increasing day by day. Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1999 and Title Execution Case No. 51 of 1992 which arc pending Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Dhaka should be disposed of on full satisfaction after making necessary note of this fact of deduction of the decreetal amount payable to the decree holder bank from the decreetal amount payable by this decree holder bank in Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1999 pending in Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka. We therefore, be disposed of on full satisfaction after making necessary note of this fact of deduction of the decreetal amount payable to the decree holder Sufia Re-Rolling & Steel Mills Ltd." with the aforesaid observations the Writ Petitions were disposed of by the High Court Division. 

 4. We have heard the submissions of the learned Advocates for the petitioners in both the petitions and also respondent in both the petitions and perused the impugned orders and all other materials on record. We have also considered the decree passed in Title Suit No. 219 of 1987 and minutely considered the words used in the decree exonerating defendant No.2 from levying any interest on him till the decree was passed in Title Suit No. 219 of 1987 i.e. 17.1.1991 till the decreetal amount is realized from the date of the judgment dated 17.1.1991. 

 5. Having considered the facts and circumstances of the case and the terms of the decree we do not find any merit in this leave petition.
